title: rosa canina var. aspernata
intro: Rosa canina var. aspernata, commonly known as wild rose or dog rose, is a shrub-like plant belonging to the family Rosaceae. The plant has been traditionally used to support various health benefits, including treating digestive issues, reducing inflammation, and alleviating symptoms of menopausal disorders, due to its potential anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antispasmodic properties. The therapeutic actions of Rosa canina var. aspernata are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which may help to regulate hormonal balance, improve circulation, and boost the immune system. The plant's extract has also been studied for its potential antioxidant and anti-cancer properties, although more research is needed to confirm its efficacy in these areas.
